title: BBC Editorial Guidelines — Section 3: Accuracy (Principles and Guidelines)

extracted.subtask_short: Judging due-accuracy and corroboration of BBC content
extracted.subtask_description: Determining whether a claim, allegation, or piece of user-generated/third-party material meets the BBC's 'due accuracy' bar — i.e., whether it is sufficiently sourced, corroborated, or must instead be attributed rather than stated as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due accuracy standard scaled to content type
rubrics_metrics.description: "Due" means the accuracy must be adequate and appropriate to the output, taking account of the subject and nature of the content, likely audience expectation, and any additional information the BBC provides that may influence that expectation. The due accuracy required of drama, entertainment or comedy is not the same as for most factual content, and can even vary within a genre — e.g., factual entertainment vs. historical documentary vs. current affairs vs. news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output must be well sourced, evidence-based, and corroborated where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: All BBC output, as appropriate to its subject and nature, must be well sourced, based on sound evidence, and where possible corroborated. Content producers should be honest and open about what they don't know and avoid unfounded speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncorroborated claims must be attributed, not stated as fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims, allegations, material facts and other content that cannot be corroborated should normally be attributed (i.e., stated as someone's claim, not as established fact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reluctance to rely on a single source
rubrics_metrics.description: Content producers should be reluctant to rely on a single source. If they do rely on a single source, it should be credible, and a named, on-the-record source is always preferable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research interviews with sources making serious allegations should, wherever practicable, be recorded; where recording might inhibit the source, full contemporaneous notes should be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroborate claims/allegations and validate documentary/digital evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate and possible, content makers should: gather material using first-hand sources; check facts and statistics, identifying important caveats and limitations; validate the authenticity of documentary evidence and digital material; corroborate claims and allegations made by contributors; weigh, interpret and contextualise claims, including statistical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose inability to verify and attribute accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Information, facts, documents and digital material must be checked and verified to achieve due accuracy — if content producers have been unable to verify material, they should usually say so and attribute the information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical claims require scrutiny, context, and range of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The same scepticism applied to sourcing should be applied to statistics — they should not be taken at face value. Numbers should be explained, contextualised, weighed, interpreted and, where appropriate, challenged; caveats and limitations should be explained; a range of evidence should be used to judge magnitude and importance; wrong or misleading claims should be challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-generated and social media content requires additional verification
rubrics_metrics.description: It should not be assumed that user-generated material is accurate — it may need verification and must always be clearly identified. Even apparently reliable internet sources may not be accurate or complete — it may be necessary to check who runs the site or confirm authenticity with an individual/organization. Additional scrutiny may be necessary if material from a social media site or other internet source is being used to corroborate a fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care is needed with content supplied by anyone with a vested interest, not just disinterested bystanders. Fact must be distinguished from rumour, especially on social media, where misinformation may be deliberate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party/agency material requires substantiation or reputable-source reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC should normally only rely on an agency report if it can be substantiated by one of its own journalists, or if it is sourced from a reputable news agency; such material should only be used if credible and reliable, with appropriate credit/attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content makers should be reluctant to use video/audio news releases or material from parties with vested interests (companies, government agencies, campaigners, charities, etc.) — this can be a route to avoid the scrutiny of an interview and may be inaccurate; any such use must be clearly labeled with who supplied it and the circumstances of production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referral test for single unnamed source making serious allegation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal to rely on a single unnamed source making a serious allegation, or to grant anonymity to a significant contributor making a serious allegation, must be referred to the Director of Editorial Policy and Standards and Programme Legal Advice before publication. The test considers: whether the story is of significant public interest; whether the source is of proven credibility and reliability and in a position to have sufficient knowledge of the events featured; whether a serious allegation was made or substantiated off the record; whether a response to the serious allegations has been sought; legal issues, safety concerns (e.g., for whistleblowers), and sensitive/personal issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform audience when allegations are not independently corroborated
rubrics_metrics.description: When allegations have not been independently corroborated, journalists should consider whether it is appropriate to inform the audience of that fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live unscripted two-ways should not normally be used to report allegations — that decision belongs to the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess credibility of linked third-party websites before linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Links should normally lead to credible sites; credibility should be assessed before linking, even where editorially justified to link to a significant site in a current story.
